title: BUN/creatinine ratio does not improve cross-cycle grip-strength prediction beyond its separately modeled components
abstract: In NHANES adults aged >=40 with complete both-hand testing, adding a BUN/creatinine spline to flexible separate-component models worsened frozen 2011-12 to 2013-14 combined-grip prediction: weighted MSE gain -0.7115 kg² (conditional 95% stratified-PSU bootstrap interval -1.0288 to -0.4349), with RMSE 11.0382 versus 11.0704 kg in 3,138 target participants. This negative model-comparison result does not refute reported muscle-health associations or exclude other nonlinear representations. Temporal sample transfer within NHANES is not external-platform validation.
